Q1: 1,1,1,2-Tetrachloroethane exhibits known significant hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, or reproductive hazards (CMR), inhalation (IHL), oral (ORL), dermal and eye (SKN), and organ and systemic (OGN) endpoints. Environmental hazards (ENV) are classified under a Tier 2 expanded perspective, while endocrine disruption (EDC) is data deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: This chemical is included on several significant "Lists of Concern," indicating recognized hazards. It is listed under California's Proposition 65 for chemicals known to cause cancer or reproductive harm, is subject to EPA's Drinking Water Standard, and is classified by IARC as a Group 2B carcinogen, meaning it is possibly carcinogenic to humans.
Q3: 1,1,1,2-Tetrachloroethane is generally well-characterized; it has a high number of scientific literature references (3,332, well above the median), a specific molecular formula (C2H2Cl4), and is classified as a "Small Molecule" rather than an incompletely defined substance. Only one of its hazard classes, endocrine disruption, is considered data deficient.
